items.title: AI Kill Switches: What Policymakers Should Know
items.excerpt: Policymakers have recently proposed requiring “AI kill switches” to quickly stop an AI system or limit the impact of a harmful or unwanted AI incident. This piece describes different potential implementations of AI kill switches at each layer of the AI stack and offers key takeaways for policymakers.

items.title: Convergent Interests: How America Could Undermine Its Own AI Advantage
items.excerpt: A convergence of political, commercial, and ideological pressures can impede America’s AI leadership, and public controversies are powerful enough to catalyze that convergence. Our piece spotlights this issue, urging policymakers to govern AI responsibly without disabling the innovation that makes American leadership possible—even in the wake of scandal.

items.title: Nearly 70 percent of US agencies use generative AI, and unions are finally catching up with guardrails
items.excerpt: US public-sector unions are increasingly pushing through protections against AI surveillance and automated firings. In Oakland, a strike vote forced retraining programs instead of layoffs, and a transport union in Ohio won veto power over autonomous vehicles. California banned so-called bossware. All of this is happening while nearly 70 percent of US government agencies already use generative AI.

items.title: Banks bar Chinese and Hong Kong investors from Anthropic IPO over US export controls
items.excerpt: Chinese investors are shut out of Anthropic's IPO, Bloomberg reports. Banks are rejecting buy orders from mainland China and Hong Kong, citing U.S. export control rules known as ITAR. Similar restrictions applied during SpaceX's IPO, and Anthropic's products aren't available in either region anyway.
